attribution: Representative paraphrased entries for UX/demo. Not official Archon/Blizzard text. Build full corpus locally with npm run corpus:build-starcraft.

entries.explanation: In each phase, the first player activates one unit, then players alternate activating a single unit at a time until both players pass.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Alternating Activations (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: The defender rolls all dice in the Armour Pool; each die meeting or exceeding the unit's Armour characteristic is discarded as a successful save.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Armour Roll (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Phase 2 of each round. Activated units may Run, Hold, Charge, or make Ranged Attacks. This is where most shooting damage and charges happen before melee.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Assault Phase (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Ranged attacks resolve through three pools: dice start in the Attack Pool (hit rolls), move to the Armour Pool, then to the Damage Pool.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Attack Pool (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Burrowed units gain HIDDEN, have Size treated as 0, and refresh HIDDEN at the start of each round while burrowed.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Burrow (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: An unengaged ground unit moves into the Engagement Range of declared enemy units, crossing open ground with a charge move.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Charge (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Phase 3 of each round. Every unit that is Engaged must fight in close combat; unlike earlier phases, these activations are mandatory for all Engaged units.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Combat Phase (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Combat Tags identify a unit's physical nature and tactical class (e.g. Armoured, Biological, Light). Many weapon keywords such as Surge and Pierce apply only against matching tags.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Combat Tag (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Terrain can grant Full Cover (blocks line of sight when the piece is large enough relative to both models) or Direct Cover (blocks LoS when a model is within 1" of terrain tall enough for that model).
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Cover (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Critical Hit (X) moves up to X dice from the Armour Pool directly to the Damage Pool, bypassing armour rolls.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Critical Hit (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Each die remaining in the Damage Pool after armour (and any Evade rolls) inflicts Damage equal to the weapon's Damage characteristic.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Damage Pool (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: A unit in Reserves enters the battlefield during the Movement Phase if its Current Supply fits within your Available Supply.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Deploy (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: After the draft picks the Mission and Deployment cards, set up the battlefield—terrain, objectives, and zones—according to those cards before Round 1 begins.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Deployment (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: An engaged unit withdraws from melee during the Movement Phase. Disengaging triggers the Tactical Mass penalty for that activation.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Disengage (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Before the battle, players draft Mission and Deployment cards from face-up options so both sides help choose what is played and where, without a preset advantage.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Draft System (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Engagement Range extends 1" horizontally from a model's base. Enemy models within that range are Engaged; if any models in two units are Engaged, both units count as Engaged.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Engagement (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: After armour rolls, the defender may Evade to discard dice from the Damage Pool. A unit with Evade (-) cannot make Evade rolls unless an ability explicitly grants one.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Evade (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Physical token tracking initiative. The roll-off winner holds it at game start; the first player to Pass in a phase takes it for the next phase.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — First Player Marker (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: When checking line of sight to or from a Flying model, ignore Full Cover. For cover purposes, treat its Effective Size as higher than any terrain on the table.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Flying (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Trace an imaginary line from any part of the attacker's base to any part of the target's base from a top-down view. If blocking terrain does not stop the line, the target is visible.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Line of Sight (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Minerals are spent during army building to recruit units and buy upgrades. Total Mineral cost cannot exceed your engagement scale limit; unspent Minerals are lost.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Minerals (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Phase 1 of each round. Units with a Movement-side activation marker may Hold, Move, Disengage, or Deploy from Reserves, then receive an Assault-side marker for the next phase.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Movement Phase (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: In the Scoring Phase, determine which units contest each Mission Marker and who controls them for victory points. A unit must meet all contesting requirements listed in the core rules.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Objective Control (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: The active player may Pass instead of activating a unit. The first player to Pass in a phase takes the First Player Marker for the next phase and cannot activate further units that phase.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Passing (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Pierce (X) often applies only against specific Combat Tags, increasing the Damage each successful die deals when the target matches.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Pierce (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Rate of Attack (RoA) is the number of dice rolled per firing model when making a ranged attack profile.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Rate of Attack (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Reaction Abilities let a player respond to specific events outside the normal activation sequence, as defined on the ability card.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Reaction (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: All units in your army list start in Reserves—not on the table. You bring them on during the Movement Phase when you have enough Available Supply.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Reserves (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: During the Assault Phase, a unit repositions without attacking—often to claim Mission Markers or improve its firing angle.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Run (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Phase 4 of each round: determine Mission Marker control, score victory points, resolve end-of-round effects, and refresh activation markers.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Scoring Phase (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: StarCraft TMG has no separate shooting phase—ranged attacks are Ranged Attack actions taken during the Assault Phase after units have moved into position.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Shooting Phase (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Sidearm weapons can be fired alongside a model's primary weapon, ignoring the normal one-weapon-per-model restriction.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Sidearm (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Each unit's Current Supply value depends on how many models it has left. The total Supply of your units on the table cannot exceed the mission Supply Pool (except in the final round, when it is unlimited).
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Supply (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: When a weapon's Surge triggers, check whether the target's Combat Tag matches the weapon's Surge Type. If it matches, move dice equal to the Surge result from the Armour Pool directly to the Damage Pool, bypassing armour; otherwise discard the Surge die.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Surge (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: A unit that Disengages suffers Tactical Mass: it cannot make Ranged Attacks during that activation.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Tactical Mass (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules

entries.explanation: Vespene Gas is spent only on Tactical Cards during army building. It cannot be converted into Minerals, and unspent Vespene is lost.
entries.citation: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules — Vespene Gas (sample)

source.documentTitle: StarCraft Tabletop Miniatures Game Core Rules
